answer: The statistically most enriched GO biological process in diseased vs control samples could not be determined in this environment: the capsule/sandbox contains no human GO-BP annotation (no R/Bioconductor, no org.Hs.eg.db/GO.db, no goa_human-style tables) and has no network access (DNS fails), so a statistically valid GO-BP over-representation analysis (ORA, Fisher exact) cannot be computed here. I deliberately do not report a fabricated GO term. The differential-expression analysis was executed in full (DESeq2-style, pure Python): 31,149 genes tested (pre-filter total≥10 across the 14 annotated samples), 7 vs 7 disease/control, size-factor normalization, shrunken per-gene dispersion, NB GLM, Wald test, BH/FDR. Primary (stable, condition-only) model, contrast disease vs control: **418 DEGs at padj<0.05 & |log2FC|≥1 (262 up, 156 down); 442 at padj<0.05 without LFC cutoff**. The sex-adjusted model (~sex+condition) is statistically degenerate on this design (single male in the disease group causes perfect separation; 19.3% of genes pinned at the LFC cap) and is documented as the sensitivity analysis. The DEG set (Ensembl + approved HGNC symbols) is ready to run a GO-BP ORA (Fisher exact; background = all measured genes with GO-BP annotation) as soon as a human GO annotation becomes available in an R-enabled environment.
